question_36499753002: I don’t want to overstate this: my documented transformer model-level work has been evaluation and interpretability research, not a production rollout. In Columbia AI Alignment Club, I worked on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B: implementing activation hooks across 28 transformer layers, linear probes, steering interventions, randomized and sham controls, grouped-bootstrap controls, and response/token-level evaluations to test whether observed logit shifts reflected reliable hallucination or refusal behavior. Separately, I have deployment-facing experience from a real-time robotics system, where I optimized inference with ONNX Runtime, quantization, asynchronous video pipelines, and integrated a locally hosted language model through Ollama into the robot control workflow. For Databricks AI FDE, I would bring the evaluation rigor from the Qwen work together with practical inference and systems integration experience.
question_37586354002: I don’t want to overstate this: I have not yet owned a direct external enterprise customer engagement on an ML/AI problem. The closest analogue is my applied ML work at Arborphy AI, where I worked through an ambiguous domain problem end to end: plant identification and botanical reasoning. I designed and evaluated vision/biological embedding architectures, built disjoint benchmarks for species identification and retrieval, created a human-review set, and developed a multi-agent botanical reasoning prototype with knowledge-graph evidence aggregation. At Columbia, I also made research code usable for non-ML wet-lab researchers through packaging, documentation, and step-by-step guides. That is the customer-facing muscle I would bring to Databricks, while being clear that enterprise client ownership would be a growth area.
